label: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 5
knowledgePattern: Combine truth counts with absolute-value implications
solution:
IV and V are exact negations, so one of them is true. Exactly one of I, II and III must therefore be true.

I implies II because y≤|y|. III also implies II because x≤|x|. Consequently neither I nor III can be the sole truth among those three, so II is true and I and III are false.

If x≥0, then |x|=x, making II and III equivalent. They cannot then have the different truth values required. Thus x<0, and the required pair is II and V. This is attainable at x=y=−1. Answer D.
